edits.current: "note": "The earlier callback report passes C 297 and C++ 283 checks. Only its ordinary C closure cases measure public lease entry, checked adapter and source body; C++ dispatch is unmeasured. The new host-reply report contributes only the contained callback-result direction. A rejected reply preserves the first boundary error, suppresses later host callbacks and leaves caller output unchanged. Lean may continue with a typed Fin-free containment value; earlier effects are not rolled back and no default Fin is substituted. Bare Fin replies and selected failure constructors needing a Fin remain refused, as do callback Subtype and checked records. This report does not establish reviewed host replies, other native hosts, recursive or generic refined replies, asynchronous or retained callbacks, or installed dispatch counters."

edits.previous: A value at or above the bound, or a negative value, returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT` with an error message naming the bound. No argument is converted and Lean is not called, so outputs and caller-owned values stay unchanged and the next call works normally. `Fin 0` parameters reject every value. Bounds wider than 64 bits are compared exactly. Results are always below their bound. Top-level parameters and results are supported, including inside `Array`, `List` and `Option` (for example `Array (Fin 10)` or `Option (List (Fin 10))`): every element is checked before Lean is called, an empty array or `none` is valid even for `Fin 0`, and a rejection names the parameter and the bound of the element that failed. Both ordinary-source and reviewed packages also check `Prod` and active `Except` branches, including arrays of products. Closed nonrecursive record and active variant fields retain their bounds through these containers. The [product reports](../evidence/native-fin-products-20261007/receipt.json), [Array reports](../evidence/native-fin-product-array-dispatch-20261007/receipt.json) and [field reports](../evidence/native-fin-records-20261007/receipt.json) record the installed C/C++ checks. Fin arguments to returned Lean closures, Lean-produced closure results and Lean-produced arguments to host callbacks also retain their bounds. The [ordinary callback report](../evidence/native-fin-callbacks-20261008/receipt.json) and [reviewed callback reports](../evidence/reviewed-callback-fin-20261008/receipt.json) cover these directions. Ordinary C/C++ host callbacks also accept Fin replies when the reply type has a Fin-free failure value, for example `Option (Fin 5)` or `Array (Fin 5)`. The C wrapper checks every active bounded leaf, and Lean independently reconstructs each Fin from a decidable proof. On rejection, the call preserves its first error, suppresses later host callbacks and leaves your output unchanged. Lean can continue internally with a typed Fin-free placeholder; previous effects are not rolled back. Bare Fin replies, reply shapes whose selected failure constructor requires a Fin, callback Subtype and checked records remain rejected. Reviewed host replies require separate installed acceptance. Generic and recursive native fields remain separate work. Source-dispatch counters were measured in C only.
